=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:611-614 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: The pre-dispatch JUDGE_JSON extraction still uses echo under xpg_echo, so RB_ACTION/RB_JUSTIFICATION/RB_FIX_DESC/RB_REMAINING can be read from corrupted JSON.
  WHY: The same printf-based xpg_echo fix was applied to close_and_reissue, but this preamble still pipes echo into jq, so a backslash-escaped judge payload can be mangled before dispatch and dropped into the default handler.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:947-948 | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, z-ai_glm-5]
  PROBLEM: merge_with_followup still extracts FOLLOWUP_TITLE and FOLLOWUP_BODY through echo into jq, leaving the same xpg_echo JSON-corruption bug unfixed.
  WHY: If echo turns backslash escapes into real newlines before jq, the follow-up fields go empty or garbled and the guard refuses a valid merge_with_followup action.
- tests/test_review_rb_judge_label_propagation.py:618-642 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The new xpg_echo regression test only covers close_and_reissue and leaves merge_with_followup untested.
  WHY: Without coverage for the follow-up path, the same echo→jq corruption bug can regress there without being caught.
- tests/test_review_rb_judge_label_propagation.py:931-980 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m2_5]
  PROBLEM: The merge_with_followup test harness still lacks xpg_echo support because the helper functions do not expose enable_xpg_echo.
  WHY: Without that flag, regression tests cannot exercise the follow-up path under xpg_echo, so the bug remains untestable.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:611-614 | severity=medium | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Pre-dispatch JUDGE_JSON extraction uses echo instead of printf, which can corrupt the JSON under bash xpg_echo.
  WHY: If xpg_echo is enabled, echo can interpret backslash escapes before jq sees them, so the extracted dispatch fields can be garbled and the judge decision can fall through unhandled.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:947-948 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The merge_with_followup branch still uses echo instead of printf when extracting FOLLOWUP_TITLE and FOLLOWUP_BODY.
  WHY: Under xpg_echo, echo can corrupt JUDGE_JSON before jq parses it, which leaves the follow-up fields empty or invalid and causes the action to be refused.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:611-614 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The pre-dispatch extraction uses echo "${JUDGE_JSON}" | jq, which can corrupt JSON under bash xpg_echo.
  WHY: When xpg_echo is enabled, backslash sequences in JUDGE_JSON are interpreted before jq runs, so RB_ACTION, RB_JUSTIFICATION, RB_FIX_DESC, and RB_REMAINING can be garbled.
- scripts/review_rb_judge.sh:947-948 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The merge_with_followup branch uses echo "${JUDGE_JSON}" | jq to extract FOLLOWUP_TITLE and FOLLOWUP_BODY, which has the same xpg_echo JSON-corruption bug.
  WHY: Under xpg_echo, backslash sequences in JUDGE_JSON are expanded before jq processes them, causing FOLLOWUP_TITLE or FOLLOWUP_BODY to be empty or garbled and triggering the refusal path.
- tests/test_review_rb_judge_label_propagation.py:618-642 (test_close_and_reissue_preserves_judge_json_bytes_under_xpg_echo) | severity=low | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The xpg_echo regression test only covers close_and_reissue and does not cover merge_with_followup.
  WHY: A future regression in the follow-up path would not be caught by the current xpg_echo test coverage.
- tests/test_review_rb_judge_label_propagation.py:931-964 (_build_merge_with_followup_harness function) | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The merge_with_followup test harness does not support xpg_echo testing.
  WHY: Without xpg_echo support in this harness, the same JSON-corruption vulnerability in merge_with_followup can regress without detection.
- tests/test_review_rb_judge_label_propagation.py:962-980 (_run_merge_with_followup function signature) | severity=low | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The merge_with_followup helper is missing an enable_xpg_echo parameter.
  WHY: That missing parameter prevents writing regression tests for the xpg_echo failure mode in the merge_with_followup branch.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m2_5 ===

  PROBLEM: Pre-dispatch JSON extraction uses echo "${JUDGE_JSON}" | jq, which can corrupt JSON under bash xpg_echo when JUDGE_JSON contains backslash sequences.
  WHY: Under xpg_echo, echo can interpret escape sequences before jq sees the data, so RB_ACTION can be empty or garbled and the case dispatch can skip handling the review-blocked decision.

  PROBLEM: The merge_with_followup branch uses echo "${JUDGE_JSON}" | jq for FOLLOWUP_TITLE and FOLLOWUP_BODY, which has the same xpg_echo corruption vulnerability.
  WHY: If xpg_echo expands backslash sequences before jq reads the JSON, FOLLOWUP_TITLE or FOLLOWUP_BODY can be empty or corrupted, triggering the missing-details refusal path even for a valid action.
